biography.plain_text: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum is the Vice President and Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates. Raised in the Al Maktoum dynasty, he became ruler of his home emirate, helping shape its expansion through aviation, trade and infrastructure. Equestrian sport and the Godolphin racing organisation form a longstanding personal interest.

long_biography.plain_text:
Prepared for public life from childhood, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum studied locally and in Britain before completing military training. He became head of the emirate’s police, then took responsibility for its airport and Jebel Ali Free Zone. These roles placed him at the centre of early state-building before he succeeded as Ruler and became UAE Vice President and Prime Minister in 2006.

His rule has focused on making the emirate an international centre for aviation, trade, tourism and public administration. Alongside government, horses have remained a serious personal pursuit: he founded Godolphin, creating an international racing and breeding organisation. The combination of institutional expansion and sustained equestrian patronage gives his public life a distinctive scale, joining dynastic succession with hands-on state leadership.
